output.brief: The rejections came from a data error in our own paperwork, not from the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane. When the new documentation system went live, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record. It carried a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of our 4.0°C specification. Every Meridane container sent through the system was set to 7°C. All five of those containers were rejected. All four containers booked by email at 4°C passed, including K5, K7 and K2, which were packed with Pellacor. Meridane's units held the setpoint we gave them, within 0.4°C, so a claim against them would fail. The Pellacor fungicide is not the cause, because K5 and K7 passed on it. Lower Serra fruit did show more decay inside the rejected containers, but that is not a reason to suspend growers. I could not tell whether it adds any risk at the correct temperature. I'm confident in this diagnosis. Do this now: correct the temperature on the mandarin product record. Have Meridane reset the container at sea, which sailed 3 Oct, and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4°C. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification before anything is submitted. Hold off on the claim, the suspension and the fungicide switch. Loggers in each container are a reasonable extra safeguard. Whether to recover costs from the contractor can wait. The logistics lead signed off the product master review on 3 Aug, so a sign-off gap is also part of this.
